assessment: stable analytic derivatives versus local automatic differentiation for edge avalanche physics

rejected_double_forward_ad.scope: four-variable Fermi-Dirac edge transport flux derivatives
rejected_double_forward_ad.failure_mode: double-precision forward propagation loses significant digits when derivatives of very large Fermi-Dirac flux factors cancel

full_local_forward_ad.decision: do not implement in the production path now
reasons: the prior double-precision implementation failed derivative and convergence gates
a dense local derivative dimension can reach the complete avalanche stencil rather than only four carrier-edge variables
every scalar operation would propagate the full local derivative vector through branch-heavy mobility, Fermi-Dirac, SG, current-reconstruction, norm, absolute-value, and limiting expressions
automatic differentiation alone does not repair cancellation in an unstable primal or derivative representation

stable_analytic_derivatives.decision: promising but gated; do not replace the accepted finite-difference path yet
stable_analytic_derivatives.preferred_scope: stable electron and hole generalized-SG transport primitives first, not the complete branch topology or reconstructed avalanche source
reasons: FermiDiracHalf is a repeated self-time hotspot and edge physics remains approximately 38 to 40 percent of production wall time
analytic primitives can avoid propagating dense derivative vectors through unrelated local variables
the implementation must preserve the current residual/Jacobian consistency and all BV, boundary, continuity, and field gates

hybrid.scope: stable analytic or narrowly scoped AD derivatives for smooth log-domain carrier-flux primitives, with the existing locally invalidated finite differences retained for non-smooth reconstruction and branch-dependent terms

required_experimental_gates: capture representative edge states from all three controlled BV benchmarks, including high-cancellation Fermi-Dirac cases
build multiprecision directional-derivative references for every affected local column
derive a stable logarithmic or scaled generalized-SG primal and derivative formulation, including generalized Einstein and Bernoulli terms
compare analytic or AD columns with multiprecision references using absolute, relative, and scale-aware error metrics before any BV solve
retain the residual-versus-Jacobian relative-error limit of 5e-4 and target no regression from the current 3.877331661396e-5 result
place the candidate behind a strict configuration guard and rerun the high-field transition before the two longer benchmarks
accept only if all three BV, boundary residual, global continuity, field-comparison, state-provenance, and performance gates pass

residual_fingerprint_decision.reason: measured active-branch fingerprint and the external process probe together remain below 0.15 percent of production wall time

final_decision.next_candidate: multiprecision-validated stable generalized-SG carrier-flux derivative primitive
final_decision.fallback: retain the accepted central-difference implementation with residual-consistent base flux caching and local invalidation
